back_translation: Your God says: "Comfort, comfort My people.

Speak gently to the heart of Jerusalem, and proclaim to her that her term of forced service is finished, her iniquity has been pardoned; for she has received from the hand of the LORD double for all her sins."
A voice of one crying out: "Prepare the way of the LORD in the wilderness; make straight in the desert Arabah a highway for our God.
Every valley will be lifted up, and every mountain and hill will be made low; the rugged, crooked ground will become level, and the rough places a plain.
And the glory of the LORD will be revealed, and all humanity will see it together." For the mouth of the LORD has spoken.
A voice says, "Cry out." And I asked, "What shall I cry?" "All flesh is like grass, and all its enduring beauty like a flower of the field.
The grass withers, the flower fades, when the breath of the LORD blows over it; surely the people are grass.
The grass withers, the flower fades, but the word of our God will endure forever."

O Zion, bearer of good news, go up onto a high mountain. O Jerusalem, bearer of good news, lift up your voice with strength. Lift it up, do not be afraid. Say to the cities of Judah: "Here is your God!"
Behold, the Lord GOD will come with might, and His arm rules for Him. Behold, His reward is with Him, and His recompense comes before Him.
He will tend His flock like a shepherd; He will gather the lambs in His arm and carry them against His chest, and He will gently lead the ewes that have young.

Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, or gauged the heavens with a single span? Who has gathered the dust of the earth in a measuring vessel, or weighed the mountains on scales and the hills with a balance?
Who has gauged the Spirit of the LORD, or as His counselor could instruct Him?
Whom did He consult for enlightenment? Who taught Him the path of justice, who taught Him knowledge, or showed Him the way of understanding?
Behold, the nations are like a single drop from a bucket and are counted as fine dust on the scales. Behold, He lifts up the islands like specks of dust.
All Lebanon is not enough for fuel, nor all its animals enough for a burnt offering to Him.
All the nations are as nothing before Him; He counts them as less than emptiness and nothingness.
To whom, then, will you compare God? Or what likeness will you set up to resemble Him?
An idol? A craftsman casts it, a goldsmith overlays it with gold and casts silver chains to adorn it.
One too poor for such an offering chooses wood that will not rot, then seeks a skilled craftsman to set up an idol that will not topple over.
Do you not know? Have you never heard? Has no one told you from the beginning? Have you not understood since the founding of the earth?
He sits enthroned above the circle of the earth, and its inhabitants are like grasshoppers. He stretches out the heavens like a curtain and spreads them out like a tent to dwell in.
He who reduces princes to nothing and makes the rulers of the earth emptiness.
Scarcely are they planted, scarcely sown, scarcely has their stem taken root in the ground, when He blows on them and they wither, and a whirlwind carries them off like stubble.
The Holy One says: "To whom, then, will you compare Me? Or who is My equal?"

Lift up your eyes on high and see: who created these? He who brings out the host of stars in procession by number, calling each of them by name. Because of His great might and strong power, not a single one is missing.
O Jacob, why do you say — O Israel, why do you declare — "My way is hidden from the LORD, and my just claim is overlooked by my God"?
Do you not know? Have you never heard? The LORD is the everlasting God, the Creator of the ends of the earth. He does not grow faint or weary; His understanding is beyond fathoming.
He gives strength to the weary and increases power for those whose strength is gone.
Even young men grow faint and weary, and strong young men stumble and fall.
But those who wait on the LORD will receive new strength. They will spread their wings and soar like eagles; they will run and not grow weary; they will walk and not faint.
